about: Hand-written tasks that the block records and the building inventory do not describe. Edit this file by hand; tools/tasks/build-board.py merges it into tasks/index.json. Fields as in tasks/README.md.

tasks.title: Finish separating the zombie game from the city
tasks.summary: Done on 2026-10-22. The city runs with no game layer (src/work/GameLayers.ts). The zombie game "Vegas: Afterlight" moved to its own project (GitFork/vegas-afterlight-game): the sanctuary and supply caches, the cast and its animations, the storm-chase film scenes, its tests, tools and design documents. It registers its layer in GAME_LAYERS. Left: the naming and the repository wiring.
items: Done on 2026-10-24: the city has its own game id PVEF9G6NJIJ6 ("Las Vegas Strip", made through the CLI's game API); the game keeps ZWLJZE4P1VA6.

Rename the city's Afterlight-named files and keys to the chosen name: AfterlightShadows.ts, the localStorage 'afterlight:film' key, window.__afterlightProbe and __afterlightFilm (tools/film and tools/probe-*.mjs use them)
After the city's first commit, make the game project a git repository whose 'city' remote is the city, and merge city updates from there
acceptance: Both projects boot and pass node tools/release/smoke-clone.mjs
The game's only change to city files is its GAME_LAYERS line

tasks.title: Record where every packed texture came from
tasks.summary: Most textures are drawn by our own scripts (tools/make-public-resort-textures.py, tools/make-arrival-materials.py, tools/strip-landmarks/luxor_obelisk_texture.py), are generated originals with recorded prompts (the Venetian interiors: docs/project-records/venetian-interiors-2026-10-23/generated-images.md) or are CC0 scans from Poly Haven. The release needs a recorded source for every packed image, or a replacement.
items: List every image packed into the runtime GLBs (tools/release/asset-pack.json) together with the script that drew it. Write the list to docs/ASSETS.md.
Check that no image in a .blend or GLB is a photo of a real property (the reference photos are for comparison only).
acceptance: docs/ASSETS.md lists each packed texture with its generator script or its licence and source URL
Anything with an unknown origin has been replaced, and the GLB re-exported and re-optimized

tasks.title: Move to the currently published engine (done: 3.1337)
tasks.summary: Done on 2026-10-24: engine 3.1337 (`bitmagic upgrade`, CLI 0.1.86). The codemod moved the engine imports; the fixes: the film atmosphere reaches the new post-FX and weather owners, the film AO and sub-frame stepping use the moved engine members, GuestDoor keeps its skin in `skin` (the engine Door now has a private `leaf`), collider vertices are `ArrayLike<number>`, reversed depth is set on the live renderer (`recreateRenderer` is gone, SkylineDepth.ts), and the batched lighting gets room for every city light (LightCaps.ts). Checked: smoke-clone (9 stops, no errors), daylight, casino and room frames match 3.1223, 60 fps at spawn. Left: the items below.
items: Game.ts is still the old whole `class VoxelGame` (deprecation warnings only): run `bitmagic upgrade --migrate-game` or follow engine/agent-docs/migrating-game-to-voxelgamebase.md

Night film looks: the engine LightManager now ranks and cross-fades street lamps (budget 32) where 3.1223 lit the nearest from a pool, so a fast night take lights different lamps; raise `lightingConfig.dynamicLights` only with the owner (it costs GPU)
Re-measure on 3.1337: tools/probe-streaming.mjs, tools/probe-interiors.mjs, tools/probe-lighting-modes.sh
acceptance: bitmagic check passes on the published engine
Frame time and stalls no worse at the probe views
smoke-clone.mjs passes

tasks.title: Publish a source pack so contributors can rebuild GLBs
tasks.summary: The runtime pack (tools/release/asset-pack.py) is enough to play and to edit code. Most builders also read files in build/: original GLBs, .blend scenes, OSM extracts and collision data. These add up to about 10 GiB. Without them, a contributor can only rebuild what a builder makes from scratch.
items: List what each builder reads from build/ (tools/strip-landmarks/build.py, export.py, tools/resort-blocks/build_*.py, tools/geographic-strip/*, tools/highrises/*, tools/level/*)
Add a `source` mode to tools/release/asset-pack.py that packs those files (no .blend1, logs, renders, before/after evidence), split into parts under 2 GiB
Make fetch-assets.mjs --source fetch and verify it
Document in docs/ASSETS.md which tasks need it
acceptance: In a fresh clone with the runtime and source packs, one strip-landmark venue and one resort block can be rebuilt, exported, optimized and loaded in the game

tasks.title: Add continuous integration: typecheck and tests
tasks.summary: Pull requests should run the typecheck and the logic tests that do not need the GPU. The engine is not in the repository: CI must install it with `bitmagic upgrade`, which needs a Bitmagic Pro login (a repository secret the maintainers control, never exposed to pull requests from forks). Some tests read build/ assets; mark those, or let CI fetch the runtime pack.
items: Find how the CLI authenticates non-interactively (a token in an environment variable) and store it as a repository secret
Run each tests/*.test.mjs in a clean clone and list which need build/ assets

Add .github/workflows/check.yml: bitmagic upgrade, pnpm install, bitmagic check, the tests that need no assets. Run it on pushes to main and on pull_request_target only after a maintainer's label, so forks never see the secret
acceptance: The workflow passes on main
A deliberate type error makes it fail

tasks.title: GPU-compressed textures (KTX2) for the city
tasks.summary: Every texture in the runtime GLBs is WebP, JPEG or PNG, so it uploads to the GPU uncompressed (python3 tools/optimize/audit-pack.py). The optimizing-assets skill can write KTX2 (ETC1S or UASTC), which stays compressed in GPU memory. The vendored engine has neither the meshopt decoder nor the KTX2 boot wait (expectGltfLoaderSupport), and the ktx tool is not installed.
items: Follow the skill (CLI assets/optimizing-assets/SKILL.md, sections 3 and 5): install the pinned ktx tool, and add the KTX2 half of the game-side shim next to src/work/GltfDecoders.ts (KTX2Loader plus the WebGPU init wait)
Start with the biggest texture sets: city atlases, landmark exteriors, hotel modules. UASTC for normal and ORM maps, ETC1S only for distant colour maps
Measure GPU memory and first-load time before and after (tools/probe-memory.mjs, tools/probe-idle.mjs)
A/B the same views with ab-compare.mjs, and show the owner the sheet
acceptance: No KTX2 or WebGPU pipeline errors in the console on a cold load
GPU memory lower at the probe views, with SSIM at or above the skill's thresholds
The owner approved the A/B sheet

tasks.title: Ship the optimized foliage to clones
tasks.summary: public/foliage/tree-0/1/2.glb (34 MiB) are committed originals. Their meshopt copies exist only in a full working checkout (build/optimized/foliage/), because glbUrl() serves a copy only when its manifest entry matches the original's size and modification time, and a git checkout resets modification times. A clone therefore loads the originals.
items: Choose between moving the tree GLBs to build/foliage/ (asset pack, out of git) and letting glbUrl() trust a pack-pinned manifest entry by size and SHA-256
Update tools/release/asset-pack.py and ResortFoliage.ts accordingly
acceptance: In a clean clone, the network panel shows the meshopt trees (about 7 MiB rather than 34 MiB)
node tools/release/smoke-clone.mjs passes

tasks.title: Lighter character downloads
tasks.summary: The nine b610x characters load from Bitmagic's CDN as originals (5.3 to 6.3 MiB each, mostly PNG textures). glTF-Transform cannot read their required BITMAGIC_sparse_correctives extension, so only a texture-only variant is possible (tools/optimize/character-textures-webp.mjs).
items: Make the texture-only WebP variants
A/B faces and skin up close
Register them and point the world.json rows at them (an upload, so the owner's approval is needed)
acceptance: Same look up close (A/B sheet approved)
Smaller download in the network panel

tasks.title: Binary collision and route data instead of JSON
tasks.summary: 203 MiB of the runtime pack is plain-text JSON: city-colliders.json alone is 118 MiB, and the venue collisions and road network add more. The game downloads and parses all of it as text. Flat Float32Array and Uint32Array buffers would cut both bytes and parse time, and follow the project's no-JS-arrays rule.
items: Write the collision vertex and index arrays as little-endian binary files beside a small JSON header (exporters in tools/geographic-strip/ and tools/strip-landmarks/export.py)
Read them as typed arrays in GeographicCity, StripLandmarks, HighriseCity and SphereVenue
Keep reading the JSON while the binary files are missing, for one release
acceptance: The same collision (walk audits pass)
Boot and first-entry stall times measured before and after with tools/probe-streaming.mjs

tasks.title: 16-bit indices where they fit
tasks.summary: 216 primitives in the runtime GLBs still use uint32 indices although they have fewer than 65,536 vertices: about 1.7 MiB of GPU index memory (python3 tools/optimize/audit-pack.py).
items: Have the optimizer driver narrow those index accessors before encoding (or have the exporters write uint16)
Re-optimize and re-pack
acceptance: audit-pack.py reports 0 uint32 index accessors that would fit uint16
Identical rendering

tasks.title: Traffic on the Strip and the streets around it
tasks.summary: The streets are empty. Cars driving the real road network would make the city feel alive (mrdoob/slop-newyork, MIT, shows how much traffic adds). runtime-assets/geographic-strip/road-network.json has 19,343 OpenStreetMap roads with their nodes, one-way flags and road classes.
items: Lanes and turns from road-network.json; signal cycles at the Strip's main intersections
A few car models, instanced (one draw per model); headlights and brake lights are emissive, never lights
Cars stop for the player and the jeep and never drive through buildings
Positions, speeds and lanes in typed arrays; deterministic from a seed so film takes repeat (tools/film/)
Nothing near interiors or far away; a density setting in the B panel
acceptance: 60 fps held at spawn and on the Strip with traffic on (tools/probe-idle.mjs, tools/probe-views.mjs)
No runtime light-set changes and no per-frame JS arrays or allocation (AGENTS.md)
node tools/release/smoke-clone.mjs passes

tasks.title: People on the sidewalks, bridges and casino floors
tasks.summary: Nobody walks the Strip. Crowds on the sidewalks, the pedestrian bridges and the casino floors would give it its scale and life.
items: Routes along the sidewalks (Clark County pavement data in the city) and the bridge concourses (GeographicPassages)
Animated people, instanced, with a far level of detail; crossings that wait for life-traffic's signals
Inside venues, light them through lightInterior() (InteriorLighting.ts) like everything else indoors
A density setting in the B panel
acceptance: 60 fps held on the Strip and in the Venetian casino with crowds on
No runtime light-set changes and no per-frame JS arrays or allocation (AGENTS.md)
Nobody walks through walls, cars or the player

tasks.title: City sound: the Strip, the casinos, the jeep
tasks.summary: The city is silent. A soundscape that follows where you are would add as much as the visuals: street hum and traffic outdoors, slot machines and crowds in the casinos, quiet hotel corridors, footsteps by surface, the jeep's engine.
items: Zones from the city's own interior and venue state (outdoors, casino, lobby, corridor, room)
Spatial sources through the engine's audio system; sounds from `bitmagic generate sound` or synthesized in code
Original or generated audio only: no recorded music and no brand sounds (the Bellagio fountains play real songs)
A volume setting and mute in the B panel
acceptance: Sound changes with the zone without gaps or pops
No runtime light-set changes and no per-frame JS arrays or allocation (AGENTS.md)
No measurable frame-time cost at spawn (tools/probe-idle.mjs)
